evals.name: ca-bundle-incident
evals.prompt: teach me PR 1875 in acme/shop — I need to understand the CA bundle thing well enough to explain it to the team on Monday
evals.expected_output: Self-contained HTML artifact teaching PR #1875. Should identify the spine (undici's `ca` option replaces Node's trust store rather than extending it, so 6 corporate certs silently dropped 144 Mozilla roots), map all 10 changed files including the 4 new ones, and include an operable element — most naturally a trust-store composition toggle.
assertions: standalone_html: one complete HTML document with no external script or style URLs
file_map_complete: every file the PR changes is named in the page
selfcheck_present: 6 to 14 predict-then-check questions in any form
interaction_simulates_model: an operable element runs this PR's own mechanism, not a quiz
page_weight_reasonable: embedded fonts stay under 120 KB and weigh less than the page content
real_error_string: quotes the real UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY error
spine_identified: explains that undici's ca option replaces Node's trust store rather than extending it, dropping the 144 Mozilla roots

evals.name: redos-regex
evals.prompt: can you help me understand https://github.com/acme/shop/pull/1872 — I'm reviewing some similar regex code and I want to actually get why the old pattern was slow, not just be told it was
evals.expected_output: Self-contained HTML artifact teaching PR #1872. Should identify the spine (the outer `*` wraps a character class that already contains `/`, so the matcher has exponentially many ways to split the same string), include a live regex input or complexity demo that actually runs both patterns, and surface the unresolved reviewer concern about the n=100 test hanging CI rather than failing.

interaction_simulates_model: an operable element runs this PR's own mechanism, not a quiz

evals.name: asyncio-lock-race
evals.prompt: walk me through PR 1874, I have to answer questions about it
evals.expected_output: Self-contained HTML artifact teaching PR #1874. Should identify the spine (asyncio.Lock only binds to a loop on its contended acquire path, so an orphaned waiter poisons the cached lock for every later caller), include a steppable timeline or interleaving explorer, and report honestly that the PR merged with changes still requested about the except-RuntimeError scope.
